It was moderately compute-heavy but still included substantial workflow overhead.

bottlenecks_identified: Timing attribution is too coarse. The conductor derives experiment durations from gaps between `[conductor]` git commits, so reported wall times mix coding, full-suite tests, doc sync, and idle gaps with the actual experiment runtime.

GPU utilization was suboptimal for paired small-model live runs. Exp 219 and Exp 221 were executed before the dual-GPU paired runner landed in Exp 225, so the two-model Qwen/Gemma workloads were effectively sequential on a 2x RTX 3090 host.

Pre-flight and post-flight validation are expensive because `run_tests()` always executes the full Python suite, and most experiment entries also rerun targeted coverage, spec coverage, integration checks, and reconciliation validation.

Documentation reconciliation is lightweight per pass but high-frequency in aggregate. Recent conductor history shows a second `Update docs for Exp ...` commit after nearly every experiment, plus extra `Update docs before planning` sync commits.

Warm-start infrastructure was not yet the default on the longest live runs. Exp 225's fresh-process dual-GPU microbenchmark only reached 1.14x speedup, which indicates cold-load and process startup overhead were still eating a large share of runtime.
improvements_suggested: Add phase-level telemetry to the conductor: record separate timings for pre-flight tests, agent implementation, live experiment execution, post-flight validation, and doc reconciliation instead of inferring everything from commit timestamps.

Default paired Qwen/Gemma benchmarks to `--parallel` on 2-GPU hosts and keep both models warm through `DualGPURunner` plus `ModelServer` so Exp 219/220/221-style workloads use both RTX 3090s continuously.

Replace universal pre-flight full-suite runs with a tiered gate: fast smoke or changed-file checks before each task, then full Python suite/spec coverage/integration on framework-changing tasks or at milestone checkpoints.

Generate ops reconciliation from structured experiment metadata instead of separate append-only doc-sync passes. Changelog/status/traceability rows should be emitted automatically from the completed experiment artifact.

Preserve warm model state across long live benchmark batches and batch inference more aggressively to cut cold-start overhead and improve dual-GPU scaling beyond the current 1.14x fresh-process result.
Run `gpu_monitor` snapshots automatically before and after long live jobs, and log per-process occupancy so idle-device regressions are caught immediately even when no >1GB zombie process exists.
